[cols="2h,5,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Curve |`secp256k1` |`ed25519` |`x25519`

|What it does
|BIP 340 Schnorr and ECDSA signatures, ECDH, the x-only tweak
|Ed25519 signatures, and Ed25519ph over SHA-512 for a message given in pieces; the X25519 secret key of a key pair
|Key agreement (Diffie-Hellman on Curve25519): two parties who exchanged public keys share a 32-byte secret

|Security level
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf[SEC 2, Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters])
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032[RFC 8032, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)])
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748[RFC 7748, Elliptic Curves for Security (X25519 and X448)])

|Key sizes
|secret 32 bytes; public 33 bytes compressed, 32 bytes x-only
|secret 32 bytes (the seed); public 32 bytes
|secret 32 bytes; public 32 bytes

|Signature sizes
|64 bytes; ECDSA in DER up to 72
|64 bytes
|none: no signatures

|Speed
|not measured yet
|not measured yet
|not measured yet

|Constant time, measured
|not measured yet
|not measured yet
|not measured yet

|Standards
|link:https://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf[SEC 2, Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters], link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki[BIP 340, Schnorr signatures for secp256k1], link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6979[RFC 6979, deterministic ECDSA nonces]
|link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032[RFC 8032, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)], link:https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final[FIPS 186-5, the Digital Signature Standard, which adds EdDSA]
|link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748[RFC 7748, Elliptic Curves for Security (X25519 and X448)]

|Ecosystems that require it
|Bitcoin (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki[BIP 340, Schnorr signatures for secp256k1]), Ethereum (link:https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf[The Ethereum yellow paper, appendix F: ECDSA on secp256k1]), Nostr (link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md[Nostr NIP-01, events signed with BIP 340 on secp256k1])
|SSH keys (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8709[RFC 8709, Ed25519 and Ed448 public keys for SSH]), Signal's signatures on its Curve25519 keys (link:https://signal.org/docs/specifications/xeddsa/[Signal, the XEdDSA and VXEdDSA signature schemes]), Tor's identity keys (link:https://spec.torproject.org/cert-spec.html[Tor's specifications, Ed25519 certificates]), Solana's accounts (link:https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts[Solana's documentation, accounts and their Ed25519 keys])
|TLS 1.3 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-4.2.7[RFC 8446, TLS 1.3, section 4.2.7 (supported groups)]), SSH (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8731[RFC 8731, Secure Shell key exchange with Curve25519]), WireGuard (link:https://www.wireguard.com/protocol/[WireGuard's protocol, cryptography]), Signal (link:https://signal.org/docs/specifications/x3dh/[Signal, the X3DH key agreement protocol])

|Browsers' WebCrypto
|no: WebCrypto offers P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519 and X25519, not secp256k1 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|yes: Ed25519 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|yes: X25519 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])

|Choose it for compatibility with
|Bitcoin's keys and signatures; Nostr's event signatures (link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md[Nostr NIP-01, events signed with BIP 340 on secp256k1]); Ethereum's ECDSA verification with a known key. Not in this version: Ethereum's recoverable signatures and its addresses from the uncompressed key; ECDH in the raw x-coordinate form of Nostr's encrypted messages (link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/44.md[Nostr NIP-44, encrypted payloads]); BIP 32's derivation (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0032.mediawiki[BIP 32, hierarchical deterministic wallets])
|SSH, Tor and Solana keys and signatures, and any protocol that names RFC 8032's Ed25519 or Ed25519ph; verification is strict (libsodium's rules), which some lenient verifiers are not. Not Bitcoin, Ethereum or Nostr, whose keys are secp256k1's
|TLS 1.3's and SSH's key exchange, WireGuard, Signal; libsodium's `crypto_box` and `crypto_kx` keys. The Ed25519 public key of a peer converts with `curves::ed25519::to_x25519_public`. A shared secret goes through a KDF before it keys a cipher. Every case of Wycheproof's X25519 file is tested (link:https://github.com/C2SP/wycheproof[Project Wycheproof, test vectors for cryptographic libraries])
